issues.description: db.sh entry duplicated — value-of-truth complected between TEMPLATE/db.sh and a local db.sh in the recipe
issues.detail: The PR both adds TAL_ZH_ADULT_TEACH=downloads to egs2/TEMPLATE/asr1/db.sh AND creates egs2/tal_zh_adult_teach/asr1/db.sh as a symlink to that same template. That's fine — but the recipe also creates local/path.sh containing nothing but MAIN_ROOT=$PWD/../../.. while a top-level path.sh symlink to TEMPLATE/asr1/path.sh already exists. Two paths to the same fact, with no documented precedence, is the textbook complecting of configuration and location. Pick one source of truth for MAIN_ROOT and delete the other.

issues.description: Transcript normalization is a chain of in-place sed mutations — place-oriented data munging that hides the actual rule
issues.detail: The transcript cleanup in local/data.sh is six chained `sed` substitutions on a stream (Ａ→A, strip #, =, 、, ，, ？, 。, trailing spaces). The *value* here is 'the set of character substitutions and deletions for this corpus' — that is data. Instead it is encoded as a sequence of shell-pipe edits, which is code that complects 'what to normalize' with 'how to walk the file.' Pull the substitution table out as a small data file (or a Python dict) and apply it once; the normalization becomes inspectable, testable, and reusable when the next TAL corpus shows up with a slightly different punctuation set.

issues.description: Hardcoded utterance counts (22467/3208/6072/29386/38924) treat a derived fact as a literal value
issues.detail: The here-doc at the bottom of data.sh asserts exact wav counts per split and exits if they disagree. The count is not an input to the recipe — it is a derived property of the downloaded archive. Encoding it as a magic number complects the recipe with one specific snapshot of the corpus and will produce a confusing hard failure if the dataset is ever re-released with a corrected utterance. Either compute the expected count from a manifest the dataset itself ships, or downgrade the check from `exit 1` to a warning. The value should live with the data, not the code.

issues.description: download_and_untar.sh repeats the same three-archive logic verbatim — incidental complexity from copy-paste, not from the problem
issues.detail: The script has three near-identical 12-line blocks for TAL_ASR-1/2/3.zip, differing only in the archive name and the sentinel directory. That is one concept (extract-if-not-already-done) expressed as three copies, which means any bugfix has to be applied in three places and the relationship between archive and output directory is implicit. Refactor to a small function `extract_if_needed <zip_name> <sentinel_subdir>` and call it three times — fewer lines, one place to fix, the mapping becomes explicit data.

issues.description: Missing-unzip path logs a warning then silently continues — error handling complected with happy path
issues.detail: Lines 9-11 check for `unzip` and print a message but do not `exit`. The script then proceeds to the archive blocks, each of which will call `unzip` and fail later with a less helpful error. The *value* of 'unzip is missing' should produce one clear failure at the top, not a confusing failure halfway through. Add `exit 1` (or document why warn-and-continue is correct here, e.g. all sentinels may already exist).

issues.description: download_and_untar.sh declares it parses arguments but does nothing on the usage path
issues.detail: Lines 13-21 print usage if argc is 0 or >2, but never `exit`. The script falls through and `$1` is then dereferenced under `set -u`, producing 'unbound variable' instead of the usage message the author intended. The intent (show usage and stop) and the mechanism (print then continue) are complected; adding `exit 1` after the heredoc separates them.

issues.description: Unquoted command substitutions in realpath calls
issues.detail: `extract_dir=$(realpath $1)` and `zip_dir=$(realpath ${2:-$extract_dir})` will break on paths with spaces. Recipe code is conventionally run on cluster paths without spaces, so this is a P2, but quoting is the simple fix: `realpath "$1"`. The complecting is small but real — argument-handling logic relies on an unstated assumption about the shape of the input value.

issues.description: README link to ASR config is wrong
issues.detail: The README writes `[./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml](./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml)` — the displayed path is correct but the link target has an extra `train/` segment that doesn't exist. The value (location of the config) is duplicated in the markdown and the two copies disagree. Cosmetic, but exactly the kind of place-oriented duplication that drifts.

issues.description: Decode config sets lm_weight: 0.7 but run.sh defaults use_lm=false — value disagrees with how it is used
issues.detail: decode_asr_branchformer.yaml carries lm_weight: 0.7, but run.sh sets use_lm=false by default, so the LM weight is dead configuration on the default path. That is fine if intentional, but the README's reported LM results imply the recipe is *meant* to be run with use_lm=true. Either flip the default in run.sh, or add a comment in run.sh that the published LM numbers require `--use_lm true`. Right now the relationship between the value and when it applies is implicit.

issues.description: Speaker ID 'one speaker per utterance' is reduced to a per-utterance synthetic spk2utt — fine but worth naming
issues.detail: The PR description claims 80+ speakers, but data.sh derives the speaker ID from the parent folder name (`TALASR$(NF-1)`), which makes every directory a 'speaker.' That is a deliberate modelling choice for an ASR recipe where speaker grouping doesn't matter much, but it complects 'true speaker identity' with 'directory layout.' If a future user reads the recipe expecting real speaker labels for SpecAugment or speaker adaptation, they will get a surprise. A one-line comment in data.sh explaining that spk is a directory-proxy, not a real speaker, would separate the value from the assumption.

review.summary: This is a standard ESPnet recipe addition — the kind that copies the egs2 template, fills in dataset-specific glue, and reports numbers. Most of the diff is incidental: symlinks, queue configs, training YAML. The interesting code is local/data.sh and local/download_and_untar.sh, both of which complect 'what the data is' (a normalization table, an archive→directory mapping, an expected count per split) with 'how to walk shell pipes.' The substitution table buried in sed pipes and the three copy-pasted extraction blocks are the clearest cases of easy-not-simple — familiar bash idioms standing in for what should be small inspectable data tables. None of this blocks the recipe from training the model (the published CER numbers say it works), so nothing rises to P0; the P1s are all 'one concept expressed across two places' or 'derived value frozen as literal.' The question that should have been asked first: what are the *values* this recipe is encoding (the normalization rule, the archive layout, the split sizes), and could they live as data rather than as steps in a shell script?
